scope: Proposition 6.1 of the manuscript “Donovan's Conjecture over Algebraically Closed Fields” (preprints/Donovans-Conjecture-over-Algebraic-Closures-of-Prime-Fields-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 203 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 80d721e72d29a9bc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix p and a defect-order bound M. Consider either a unipotent block of GLn(q) or GUn(q) of defect order at most M, or a block in a sign-parameter series of an original regular classical group above, before extraction, whose defect order modulo its central p-subgroup is at most M. There are constants depending only on p, M with the following properties. The required Cartan bound reduces to Cartan bounds for groups with root data in a finite set, and for the following block-union projections: labels in a fixed ordinary cuspidal triangle series, with a bounded number of split Harish–Chandra rank-one steps above the triangle. The latter projections have boundedly many basic rows and bounded block defects, although the triangle rank can be unbounded. The transfer constants are uniform. Consequently Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 7.1 give the required Cartan bounds for all these blocks.
